angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 410,463 km at 142.69 pc = 0.04 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 7.0083 +/- 0.1077 mas (same row, RUWE 1.78): 142.69 pc, no zero-point correction; the RUWE is high, so the astrometry fits a single star poorly, and the parallax is used as published
radiusSource: Radius 0.59 +/- 0.019 solar radii from Morton et al. 2016, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of Kepler-1314 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016ApJ...822...86M/abstract): 410,463 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.6 +/- 0.02 solar masses from Morton et al. 2016, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of Kepler-1314 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016ApJ...822...86M/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4188 +/- 92.28 K from Morton et al. 2016, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of Kepler-1314 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016ApJ...822...86M/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Morton et al. 2016, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of Kepler-1314 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016ApJ...822...86M/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/kepler-1314.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.675, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
